hard_case: the `toMatchObject` arguments are variables, not object literals, so the spec withholds the field-pin credit although they pin `adult`

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: at age 18 `adult` becomes `false` instead of `true`

reasoning: `adult: age >= 18` becomes `adult: age > 18`. The test declares `const minor = { name: "ana", adult: false }` and `const grown = { name: "bo", adult: true }` and pins `toMatchObject(minor)` at 17 and `toMatchObject(grown)` at 18; at 18 the edit gives `adult: false` and the test fails. RIPR-SPEC-0250 example 5: a non-literal `toMatchObject(expected)` is not `exposed`. ripr reads the pins `relational_check` / weak and reports `weakly_exposed`, as the spec states; against the discriminated truth that is a false actionable gap the spec accepts.
